- 2026-10-02 10:05 key 20261002T0754-rknh by unrecorded · 075 review changes · by rev-runes-016 (fresh) · Important: part a regresses an edge 1.0.0 reports. When a web node declares the global Program explicitly ('public partial class Program { }', the documented WebApplicationFactory pattern for .NET 6-9) and ANY other node has top-level statements (Aspire AppHost, a worker, a migrator), the implicit key from that other file makes 'Program' two-owner ambiguous and the test -> web edge goes silent. Repro <the session scratchpad, since lost>/patch-611/review-016-csharp-refs/after/probe/partial.mjs (web top-level + partial, apphost top-level, tests WebApplicationFactory<Program>): base edge tests -> web at ApiTests.cs:4, branch []. Real repo: bug-hunt verify-44 ca-partial-web (CleanArchitecture with the partial in Web) under yg 6.1.0: base reports Application-FunctionalTests -> Web at WebApiFactory.cs:10, the branch's csharp.mjs drops it. The same holds for a classic global 'class Program { static Main }' next to any top-level file elsewhere. This is a behaviour trade-off patch-scope sends to the owner, and the changelog fragment hides it ('stays silent' reads as no change). Either avoid it (let the implicit Program yield to an explicit global Program, e.g. publish it under an internal fallback key that the bare 'Program' reference tries only after the verbatim key is absent; no new export needed), or ask the owner and state the lost edge in the fragment.

- 2026-10-02 10:17 key 20261002T0722-lboi by unrecorded · 011 review changes · by rev-runes-010 (fresh) · Important: holds() passes the default include (no files, no include) through asDirectory(configDir), and asDirectory treats a last segment with a dot as a file pattern, so a config in a directory like apps/web.v2 holds nothing by default; tsc's default is **/* under the config and ignores the name. Effects, each checked against tsc 6.0.3 --listFilesOnly: (a) regression on a non-solution layout, a false edge: apps/web.v2/tsconfig.json with its own paths @/* -> ./src/*, no include, references ./tsconfig.node.json (include **/*.ts, paths -> ./build/*): 1.0.0 and tsc give apps/web.v2/src/m.ts, the branch gives apps/web.v2/build/m.ts; (b) a solution root in a dotted dir whose default-include config and a second config both hold the file with different paths: tsc has two disagreeing holders (ruling: silence), the branch binds the second; (c) a lone default-include referenced config in a dotted dir is never a holder (silence). Fix, verified to cure all three: const include = config.include ?? (config.files === undefined ? [configDir === '' ? '**/*' : `${configDir}/**/*`] : []); plus a unit test. Repro: scratchpad patch-611/review-010-ts-resolve/probe011/probe2.mjs (S14) and probe.mjs (S1, S5).

- 2026-10-02 10:48 key 20261002T0958-hsbn by unrecorded · 149 review changes · by rev-runes-135 (fresh) · Important: CRLF regression in tomlLogicalLines + KEY_VALUE. A joined logical line keeps each line's \r (only the \n becomes a space), and KEY_VALUE's (.*)$ cannot cross a \r, so any CRLF entry whose inline table holds a multi-line array no longer matches at all. Before 5be4794 the first physical line was read; now the whole entry is dropped: kit = { workspace = true, features = [\r\n "x",\r\n] } (zed's crates/zed gpui_platform shape) or a path written before the array loses the crate, and the 149 shape itself (path after the array) is still silent on CRLF. Evidence: disk-backed CRLF workspace (<the session scratchpad, since lost>/patch-611/review-135-cargo-manifest/crlf-ws, crlf-edge.mjs): kit::Engine from crates/app/src/main.rs binds crates/kit/src/lib.rs on fbc0539 and is undefined on 462c70c. The worker's 344-file corpus converted to CRLF (diff-cargo-eol.mjs, corpus-crlf.log): base 2 disagreements with smol-toml, head 31 new (17 workspace deps in zed/Cargo.toml incl. reqwest, gpui_platform workspace=true in crates/zed, xim and 6 more in gpui_linux, ...); LF stays new=0 fixed=2. A Windows checkout with autocrlf gives exactly this. Fix: treat \r\n as the newline in tomlLogicalLines (or let the value capture [\s\S]*), plus a CRLF unit case (path before and after a multi-line array).

Probes, base -> head: [lib] path=lib.rs + [[bin]] path=main.rs, crate::Config from library module foo.rs: lib.rs -> main.rs (decoy, main.rs shadows Config); crate::LibOnly: lib.rs -> undefined. [lib] path=lib/lib.rs + [[bin]] path=main.rs: crate::Item from lib/util.rs: lib/lib.rs -> main.rs (decoy); crate::util from lib/other.rs: lib/lib.rs -> util.rs (the binary's module, decoy). [lib] and [[bin]] both in crates/core: crate::Item from crates/core/util.rs: crates/core/lib.rs -> undefined. Fix: let the library root's directory compete in the deepest-directory choice (a file under the lib's directory keeps the library tree; same directory as a bin -> both roots, like src/'s [lib, main], or fail closed).

- 2026-10-02 12:11 key 20261002T0737-hcph by unrecorded · 048 review changes · by rev-grain-048 (fresh) · Important: cb3e416 moves file co-change for completeness, check, review, the hooks and where from the whole history to the newest 20 000 non-bulk commits. Before, model.cochange/nonMegaCommits/fileTouches came from the walk's running counts (history.mjs replay: state.pairSup/fileCommits/fileOthers, never truncated); now applyFileCochange counts H.fps, which history.mjs truncates to CFG.fpsCap = 20000. This is a new limit for these surfaces (grain cochange always had it). On any repository with more than 20 000 non-bulk commits, partners whose co-change is older than the window vanish and every count and base rate shifts. Shown on scratch copies of both trees with fpsCap lowered to 30 (x.js+y.js together 10 times, then 40 other commits): release/6.1.1 names y.js 11/11, the branch names nothing (scratch: <the session scratchpad, since lost>/patch-611/review-048-cochange-one-population, make-old.sh, cap30-*). Not asked by the acceptance, not raised to the owner (patch-scope: a behaviour change with a real trade-off goes to him as a question), absent from the changelog entry, and docs/mathematics.md:292 still says fpsCap is a compute guard on which no claim rests. An alternative exists: footprints list only the new path of a rename (fps {files:[mid/a.js], renames:[[src/a.js, mid/a.js]]}), so the walk's un-floored full-history counts could be carried through currentPathOf before the floor, with its own edge cases (a commit naming two historical paths that resolve to one). Either ask the owner and disclose the window in the changelog and mathematics.md, or keep the full-history population.

So when an edit turns a declaration's only (or topmost) decorator into a comment or a blank line, or deletes it while a comment sits between it and the declaration, the declaration is no longer in the change and the deviation the edit made is filed as pre-existing. Fixture cart.handler.ts line 6 '@Handler()' -> '// @Handler()': before '1 deviation(s) in your change', and the check-hook says 'Your type CreateCartHandler (line 7) is not annotated with @Handler'; after '0 deviation(s) in your change, 1 pre-existing' and the hook is silent. The same happens when line 6 is blanked, and when '@Handler()' is deleted with '// eslint-disable-next-line ...' committed between it and the class. Real repo, flask d73fa1c tests/conftest.py:37 '@pytest.fixture' -> '# @pytest.fixture': before '1 deviation(s) in your change ... Your method app_ctx (line 38) is not annotated with @pytest.fixture' and the hook speaks; after '0 deviation(s) in your change, 2 pre-existing' and the hook gives only the co-change line. Acceptance 3 ('a change to or a deletion of the @Handler() itself is still attributed to the class') fails for the commonest way to switch a decorator off. By construction the same holds for Java/C#/Kotlin/PHP annotations: once commented out, the comment sits outside the declaration's node. The tests cover only a decorator swapped for another (D) and a deletion directly above the class (D2). Possible fix: also count a hunk whose removed lines lay on the scope's stack at HEAD (the pre-image), or let the head extend over the comment lines directly attached to it.

Reproduced: lock '99999\nsome-container' -> grain status still waiting after 6 s. With a 30 s heartbeat the foreign-host staleness window can be a few heartbeats; release on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP; name .grain/cache/build.lock in the waiting line. Hooks are not affected (they never take the lock; check-hook exit 0 while the lock was held).

A TypeScript declaration file without import/export (global.d.ts, env.d.ts: 'declare global {...}', 'interface Foo {}') gets g=typescript, esm=false, directive='none'. The result is a false-red after adoption on a file where the directive means nothing, and the changelog line 'no longer counts TypeScript ... files' is false for it. The fill runs the script but writeOrRemoveSplitFile refuses to write .yg-lock.deterministic.json, so even this run's own verdicts are thrown away. A fresh container checkout with dubious ownership plus script rules is therefore always red. Suggest: when git can't be asked, distrust only what was on disk before the run (or skip just the read) while still writing and using this run's own verdicts. Or decide to accept the red and put it in the Before-you-upgrade note.

Probe on the tip: a conflicted merge finished with git commit, then 'yg check --approve' run straight away exits 0, PASS, and closes the cycle. The following 'yg check' is PASS, the merged log keeps a branch's entry as its newest, and the owed entry was never asked for. That is the very 'easy to skip' of the Why. --approve has to refuse (or stop at) the same unreconciled merge the plain check flags.

- 2026-10-04 22:55 key 20261002T1101-mmvb by unrecorded · 166 review changes · by rev-ygg-166 (fresh) · Important: nested re-include of a DIRECTORY is not honoured for files below it. Repro (from fuzz vs git check-ignore --no-index, git 2.55, tracked and untracked, ignorecase true and false): root .gitignore 'a/', Sub/.gitignore '!a/', file Sub/a/n.txt -> git keeps it, isFileGitignored=true and walkRepoFiles drops it. Same with root 'build/' + b/gen/.gitignore '!*/'. Cause: stackIgnores asks each layer about the leaf, and node-ignore's test() checks the leaf's parent dirs inside that shallow layer ('a/' matches), so the shallow layer's inherited verdict wins after the deeper layer already re-included the directory; the ancestor loop got the directory right. Fix direction: once the ancestor loop clears every ancestor, a layer's verdict that comes only from a parent directory must not count (e.g. skip a layer whose test(parentDir/) is ignored). Add that case to the parity test.

- 2026-10-05 14:58 key 20261004T2055-pjbm by unrecorded · 221 review changes · by rev-ygg-221 (fresh) · Important — (b) is a false red: after a rebase, the entry the message asks for, committed without a fill (the documented log-cycle-open state), is still log-entry-missing in every clone, and yg check --approve refuses over it (reproduced: log add, commit, check FAIL, approve exit 1). To clear it the user has to write a second entry and fill before committing. The message says the newest entry 'was committed with that history rather than written for it', which is false here, and the CHANGELOG line 'an entry of its own settles it' is false once committed. The node log says a replayed entry and a later one cannot be told apart, but they can: a replayed entry predates the combining commit's committer date, and a later entry postdates it.

The cli-lock-scope budget of 180 s only stops a hung case: every assertion is unchanged, and the global testTimeout of 30000 still covers the rest; the other heavy e2e suites use 240 s. reference-truth and lock-scope pass 9/9 on the tip.

- 2026-10-08 11:45 by unrecorded · asked a-018 (charter) · 6.2.0 growth, all of it in one question (the design research/2026-10-08-jarl-field-report-and-repository-names/design.md, Proposed changes, built on a field report from a loop in another project): beyond the Jarl scope you approved in a-002, the design proposes (1) in 246, that a merge no longer records its CI as pending by default but only when a run will report, that a merge which lands while its check is red for a cause outside the branch is recorded with --red naming the issue that tracks the cause, and that whether a repository lands on its check is derived from its merge rows instead of a declared Check line; (2) in 244, that one answer can settle several ratify items with one verdict, and that superseding a ruling names the open issues that still cite it; (3) in 250, that the sentence "a compaction is a session start" also goes into the instructions Jarl's MCP server gives the host; (4) issue 280, that show prints by default only what the done gate counts (every row and verdict since the last start, every unanswered finding) and show --full the whole file. Options: (a) all four into 6.2.0: the Jarl part of the release grows, and 247 stays the first item to set aside; (b) none, they go to 6.3.0: until then a merge's CI stays pending or none, both false for a merge that is not pushed, an outside red is charged to the worker as a round, and show grows with 248's full reviews; (c) choose item by item. Recommendation (the architect's design): (a); it proposes every item for 6.2.0 and names the bounded show explicitly, because 248, already in 6.2.0, makes show grow faster.

- 2026-10-11 20:26 by unrecorded · decided hooks-silent-while-refreshing · by jarl
- 2026-10-11 20:26 key 20261005T1413-vrdd by unrecorded · 228 evidence · Ruling hooks-silent-while-refreshing: While a hook-started refresh runs, the edit-time hooks answer nothing; they emit no status marker. The acceptance allows the rest to wait or answer with a marker, and the release plan's defaults allow a marker or silence while refreshing, never the old index. A marker on every edit would put a line into the agent's context on each tool call for the seconds or minutes a refresh takes, and SessionStart already says that the hooks are silent while the index is behind. Waiting would stall the edit. Silence is therefore the answer, and the documentation says so.

- 2026-10-29 14:33 by unrecorded · asked a-026 (charter) · Issues 346 to 354 make every family repository leave only code on the host, and their pattern puts loop workers in clones on a container volume instead of worktrees. The ruling worktrees-follow-gard puts worktrees in .worktrees of the shell on the host, mounted at the same path in the container, which removes the reason for clones (a worktree made inside a container left dangling entries in the host's git) and keeps the rule, because a worktree is code. Options: (a) 346 to 354 adopt Gard's layout and wait for Gard's run and worktree issues (379, 387), so the family moves once; (b) 346 to 354 go ahead now with clones on a volume, and 424 later moves the family to Gard's layout; (c) 346 to 354 do the dev containers now without the worker part, and the worker part waits for Gard. The jarl recommends (c): containers that leave the host clean are needed now for the release's checks, and the workers' place is decided once, by Gard.

- 2026-11-02 21:49 key 20261011T2055-rsvv by unrecorded · 295 review changes · by rev-runes-295-opus (fresh) · Important: the diff makes item 1 of the folded evidence worse in one shape, so item 1 belongs to this issue: namespace A { using O = X.Order; class C { O x; } } namespace B { using O = Y.Order; class D { O y; } } with a global type O now gives the use in A an edge to the global O (false edge); on release/1.1.0 that use was silent. Cause: aliases and aliasScopes are keyed by name and the last directive wins (src/relations/extractors/csharp.mts:505-506), viewAlias then finds B's body outside A and returns undefined, so the verbatim reading binds. Fix: keep one alias entry per directive body and pick the one whose body encloses the use; add a catalogue case for both shapes (with and without a global O) · Minor: item 7 is half done: 13.4 became 14.5 but 13.3 (namespace declarations) and 13.8 (qualified alias member) remain catalogue-wide, and the new case csharp-alias-colon-colon-in-namespace-edge cites 13.8 · Minor: items 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 are untouched behaviour that predates this change; they can split into a new 6.2.0 issue · Acceptance tests 1-3 met, red on the base extractor (3 fail) and green on the branch (140 pass), reproduced · model claude-opus-5-5
